te: Meeting 6/2569 · Subcommittee to Study Breed Improvement and Integrated Marketing Strategy Development for Beef Cattle to Increase Competitiveness
Draft report discussed: external and internal factors affecting the beef cattle industry
se: The meeting considered the report on "Breed Improvement and Integrated Beef Cattle Marketing Strategy Development to Increase Competitiveness" and discussed the situation of the beef cattle industry. On external factors, it felt that trade liberalisation and unlawful imports affect domestic prices, and proposed preventive measures and serious law enforcement. On internal factors, it found that production is still small-scale and scattered, so costs are high, quality is uneven and farmers lack bargaining power
it: Study report on Breed Improvement and Integrated Beef Cattle Marketing Strategy Development to Increase Competitiveness

te: Outline of the 4-chapter study report on beef cattle considered
se: The meeting considered the draft report on "Breed Improvement and Integrated Beef Cattle Marketing Strategy Development to Increase Competitiveness", which has 4 chapters: introduction; the situation and problems of beef cattle in Thailand and the world, with examples of foreign policies; study methods; and study results with recommendations
it: Draft study report on Breed Improvement and Integrated Beef Cattle Marketing Strategy Development to Increase Competitiveness

te: Beef cattle exports and imports studied, and a disease-control compartment approach proposed
se: The meeting considered the laws and mechanisms for beef cattle exports and imports. It proposed that the Department of Livestock Development consider changing its disease-control approach from making the whole country or whole zones disease-free to a "compartment" system, that is, specific disease-control areas, as in the pig and chicken industries, so that beef can be exported from controlled areas without waiting for the whole country to be disease-free. It also considered the related legal and regulatory obstacles
it: Proposal to use specific disease-control areas (compartments) for beef exports
Legal and regulatory obstacles to exports and imports

te: Problems and proposals on slaughterhouses and meat processing studied
se: The meeting considered the laws and oversight mechanisms for slaughterhouses and meat processing. It found that the standards and oversight system still lack flexibility and do not fit the varied contexts of production, and it felt that food safety standards should rest on the same basis so that consumers in Thailand are protected equally
it: Situation, problems and policy proposals on slaughterhouses and meat processing

te: Laws along the beef cattle chain studied: production and middlemen
se: The meeting set a framework to study the laws along the beef cattle chain in 5 stages: breed improvement, production, middlemen, slaughter and processing, and imports and exports. It then considered the production and middleman stages. The main production issues are farmer grouping, animal movement and the use of beta-agonists (lean-meat enhancers). The meeting felt that promoting all farmers in the same way may not suit the real context of each group
it: Framework for studying the laws along the beef cattle chain in 5 stages
Problems and laws in the production and middleman stages
